facts.text: Dad George is played by Robert Carradine, and his son Isaac by Jake Thomas. They'd already played a TV family on Disney's Lizzie McGuire and its 2003 movie.
Watch the house sign as the family arrives: the numbers flip upside down and read 666.
Vanessa Angel (mom Claire) was the original pick to play Xena: Warrior Princess. She got sick and couldn't fly to New Zealand, so Lucy Lawless, already there, got the part.
Robert Carradine is best known as Lewis Skolnick in Revenge of the Nerds (1984). He was also the youngest of seven brothers and the last to enter the film business.
The creepy Dean is played by Bob Thomas, who is the real-life father of Jake Thomas, the actor playing Isaac standing before him.
Brock, the jock who stuffs Isaac in a locker, is played by Matthew Lawrence, who was Chris Hillard, Robin Williams' son in Mrs. Doubtfire (1993).
Jake Thomas (Isaac) won a Young Artist Award in 2002 for supporting actor as Martin Swinton in Steven Spielberg's A.I. Artificial Intelligence.
The math-test student Christian Salazar also appeared in The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift, released the same year as this movie.
Taylor Dooley (Dana) is also Lavagirl in Robert Rodriguez's 2005 3-D film The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl, which grossed $72 million against a $50 million budget.
Taylor Dooley was named after singer Taylor Dayne. Her Sharkboy and Lavagirl co-stars include Taylor Lautner, who is also a real-life friend.
Matthew Lawrence (Brock) co-starred with his real-life brothers Joey and Andrew in the 1995 sitcom Brotherly Love, and later played Jack Hunter on Boy Meets World.
Robert Carradine's Revenge of the Nerds cable making-of short showed him breathing gas before takes to create Lewis Skolnick's famous laugh.
Quentin Tarantino originally wrote the role of Clarence Worley in True Romance (1993) with Robert Carradine (George here) in mind.
Musetta Vander (Miss Morticia) and Jake Thomas (Isaac) both appeared in The Cell (2000), the Jennifer Lopez serial-killer thriller, six years before reuniting for Halloween silliness.
Producer Lorenzo Doumani is the son-in-law of Don Epperson, according to IMDb.
Vanessa Angel is best known for TV's Weird Science and Stargate SG-1, and for co-starring in the 1996 comedy Kingpin.
The Hollywood Walk of Fame runs about 1.3 miles along Hollywood Boulevard. The first permanent star, for producer Stanley Kramer, was set in 1960.
Rotten Tomatoes lists Leslie Allen as director and Lorenzo Doumani as producer. Some databases credit Doumani as director, so even the credits are a bit haunted.
Jake Thomas starred as Matt McGuire on Lizzie McGuire from 2001 to 2004, then played Jason Stickler on Cory in the House.
Alan Rachins, who plays Professor Skuttlebutt, was Douglas Brackman Jr. on L.A. Law for 171 episodes and earned Golden Globe and Emmy nominations. He was also Dharma's dad on Dharma & Greg.
The movie was shot in Los Angeles, which suits its Hollywood Boulevard and Walk of Fame scenes.
Alan Rachins (Professor Skuttlebutt) voiced the Clock King in Batman: The Animated Series and Norman Osborn in The Spectacular Spider-Man. He was also a Mensa member.
Rotten Tomatoes lists no critic reviews for Monster Night, only a 45% audience score. It's a straight-to-video Halloween cult curio.
The observatory in this scene appeared in Rebel Without a Cause (1955). A bust of that film's star, James Dean, now stands on the grounds. The observatory opened in 1935.
Alan Rachins, playing Professor Skuttlebutt, left the Wharton School to study acting. He later won a place in the American Film Institute's writing and directing fellowship.
Robert Carradine, who played George Ackerman here, died on February 23, 2026. He came from the Carradine acting dynasty founded by his father, John Carradine.
Musetta Vander (Miss Morticia) played Sindel in Mortal Kombat Annihilation (1997) and the She-Mantis in the Buffy the Vampire Slayer episode Teacher's Pet.
Vanessa Angel started a 1970s-inspired clothing line, VANE la, in 2009, sold in top Los Angeles boutiques.
Musetta Vander was born in Durban, South Africa. She was a Siren in O Brother, Where Art Thou? and a henchwoman in Wild Wild West (1999).
Taylor Dooley began making a movie with the other kids on the set of The Adventures of Sharkboy and Lavagirl 3-D.
Sharkboy and Lavagirl got poor reviews and flopped, but has since gained a cult following. A sequel, We Can Be Heroes, came out in 2020.
